title: More than one: the T-plural
summary: Use the nominative plural ending -t for people and things that are the subject of a basic sentence.
objectives: Add -t to a stable noun stem.

sections.title: Singular, plural, and nominative
paragraphs: Singular means one: yksi kissa, one cat. Plural means more than one: kissat, cats.
Nominative is the basic subject form. A subject is the person or thing that the sentence is about. The Finnish nominative plural usually ends in -t.

sections.title: The regular construction
paragraphs: For a stable word, start with the singular and attach -t directly. The -t itself does not have a vowel, so vowel harmony does not choose between two versions.
Some nouns need KPT before -t. The next lesson separates that stem change from the plural ending.

steps: The singular stem kissa- stays unchanged.
The singular stem ystävä- stays unchanged.
Keep ä; the plural ending is only t.

commonMistakes: Do not add English -s to a Finnish word.
Do not change a final a to ä; preserve the vowels of the noun.
The T-plural is one plural form; later Finnish cases use other plural construction patterns.

practiceExercises.explanation: The stem stays kissa-. Add plural -t: kissat.
The singular pallo has a stable stem. Add -t: pallot.
Add plural -t directly to ystävä: ystävät.
